014.craft: Kyoto has worked lacquer for more than a thousand years. Kyō-shikki is built coat by coat from the sap of the urushi tree, each layer left to cure before the next goes on.
014.marketNote: Kōbō-san, held in the grounds of Tō-ji on the 21st of every month — one of Japan's oldest flea markets.

015.craft: Weavers from the Atlas still bring their rugs down to the medina. Each pattern is carried in memory, not on paper, so no two looms make the same thing twice.
015.marketNote: The old square at the heart of the souks, north of Jemaa el-Fna, where carpets are still traded.

016.craft: The valleys around Oaxaca hold some of Mexico's oldest pottery traditions. In San Bartolo Coyotepec the clay is burnished by hand with a stone and fired to the black that made it famous.
016.marketNote: The old market of the historic centre, steps from the zócalo.

017.craft: Athens has worked silver since antiquity — the mines at Laurion paid for its fleet. Its jewellers still gather in the streets below the Acropolis.
017.marketNote: On Ifestou Street, named for the god of the forge.

018.craft: London's stone was carried in from the quarries. Portland limestone faces St Paul's and much of the city rebuilt after the Great Fire.
018.marketNote: London's best-known antiques market, on Saturdays in Notting Hill.

003.craft: Painted tile reached Lisbon in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and never left. Whole façades of the city are still clad in azulejos.
003.marketNote: Lisbon's flea market on the Campo de Santa Clara, Tuesdays and Saturdays.

007.craft: Jaipur's armourers worked for the Kachwaha court. The katar, a dagger gripped in the fist, was a blade of Rajput nobility.
007.marketNote: Across the middle of the walled Pink City, laid out as a grid in 1727.

009.craft: In Kerala the brass lamp is lit at the threshold at dusk. Mannar, a town in Alappuzha, has cast bell metal for generations.
009.marketNote: Where lamps and temple vessels are still cast by hand.

012.craft: In the Andes, weaving is a language: patterns passed from mother to daughter, spun from alpaca and sheep's wool, coloured with plants and cochineal.
012.marketNote: Cusco's central market, a few blocks from the Plaza de Armas.

019.craft: Japanese blades are forged and folded in layers. Patterned-steel kitchen knives carry that grain in every edge.
019.marketNote: Tokyo's kitchen-tool street, between Ueno and Asakusa, lined with knife shops.

020.craft: Murano's millefiori glass found a second home in Scotland, where twentieth-century makers in Perthshire and Caithness took up the paperweight.
020.marketNote: Aberdeen's old market place, marked by the Mercat Cross since 1686.

021.craft: The rya began as a working blanket on Nordic boats and beds — a long knotted pile to keep the cold out — before it moved to the wall.
021.marketNote: The Sunday flea market in Grünerløkka's park.
